title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 379
paragraphs: There are seven classes of Egyptians: one is called that of the priests, another that of the warriors, and the rest are cowherds, swineherds, shopkeepers, interpreters, and boatmen. This is the number of the classes of the Egyptians, and their names are given them from the occupations they follow. Of these, the warriors are called Calasirians and Hermotybians, and they come from the following districts — for all Egypt is divided into districts.
